title: Screen-space lane chrome is set in world type: 14 selectors at 7 and 9 px
body:
## Summary
The title readout, toolbar, story bar, cards, lane rail and script rail are HTML in screen space, yet they take their type from the WORLD tokens --al-text-tag (0.4375rem, 7 px) and --al-text-sub (0.5625rem, 9 px), under the app's smallest chrome token --at-text-micro (11 px).

## Description
lanes.css defines --al-text-label/sub/tag as world lengths: its header says they agree with geometry.ts because the camera scales the world (examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:7-10, :41-43). Fourteen selectors that the camera never scales use them: .al-title-read dt (examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:164), .al-card li (:708), .al-tool (:733), .al-story-chapter (:786), .al-story-n (:804), .al-story-what (:816), .al-story-cite (:823), .al-story-receipt (:833), .al-lane-rail-ord (:1087), .al-lane-rail-note (:1107), .al-script-n (:1156), .al-script-label (:1174), .al-script-where and .al-script-cite (:1187-1188). Eight of them render at 7 px and six at 9 px at every zoom, below --at-text-micro (11 px, components/atlas/style/base/tokens.css:73). The toolbar and chapter buttons are about 19-21 px tall at that type (4 px + 8 px padding, 1 px borders), under the WCAG 2.5.8 24 px target. Fixed looks like: screen-space chrome reads --at-text-micro / --at-text-label, world tokens stay inside .al-sheet; a lanes.css test can hold that split.

## Flow
- Open /?variant=archify-lanes at 1440x900; read the story bar's chapter buttons and cite, or the title band's level/phase/scale captions
- lanes.css resolves them to --al-text-tag: 7 CSS px, unscaled, because they sit outside .al-world
- Fix: swap the 14 chrome selectors to --at-text-micro/--at-text-label, then re-measure the canvas height at 1440x900 and the editorial script rail (max-height 9.5rem)

## Expected impact
Every reader of the three finishes; the chrome becomes legible at the app's own floor. What could break: taller chrome shrinks the canvas, and home is clamped at scale 1 with no fit pass, so the sheet could clip at 1440x900 (lanes.routing.test.ts estimates the canvas at about 600 for a 578-unit world).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - screen-space text and targets at the app's own type floor
Before: 14 screen-space selectors on world type tokens (8 at 7 px, 6 at 9 px); 0 at or above --at-text-micro
After: probe on the stylesheet: 0 of 14 below 11 px once swapped; the canvas height at 1440x900 is the unmeasured half
Method: probe - selectors counted from lanes.css; a gate is not reachable because whether the sheet still fits its canvas at 1440x900 needs a real browser, which this round does not drive
Result: better
Gate: none (Lane C: needs a browser to see the 1440x900 fit)
evidence:
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:164 .al-title-read dt font-size: var(--al-text-tag)
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:733 .al-tool font-size: var(--al-text-sub)
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:786 .al-story-chapter font-size: var(--al-text-tag)
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:43 --al-text-tag: 0.4375rem; /* 7 */
components/atlas/style/base/tokens.css:73 --at-text-micro: 0.6875rem;

title: The story bar clips the beat sentence instead of fitting it
body:
## Summary
.al-story-what is nowrap with overflow hidden and text-overflow clip, so a beat sentence wider than its flex slot is cut mid-word, in a drawing whose stated rule is that text shrinks or is rejected and never clips.

## Description
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css:816-820 sets .al-story-what { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: clip; white-space: nowrap }. text.ts:2-12 and Scene.tsx's header state the drawing's rule: no ellipsis, no clip, a string that cannot be drawn is a fact about the wording. The beat sentences (script.ts SCRIPT labels, up to about 33 characters, plus the node label and cite in the same row) fit at 1440 but share a flex row with the receipt and controls (.al-story flex-wrap). Wrapping instead of clipping makes the bar's height vary by beat, which resizes the canvas through the flex column and moves the ResizeObserver frame every step; so the fix is a decision between one line that fits (shorter copy or a fixed slot) and a two-line bar of constant height.

## Flow
- Open the TURN story at a 900-1100 px wide window and step through the twelve beats
- A long beat ("reversible? external? -> GATED" beside "The catalog" and its cite) loses its tail with no ellipsis and no hint
- Fix candidates: reserve two lines for .al-story-what at constant height, or test the beat strings against the slot like text.ts tests node labels

## Expected impact
Readers on narrower windows following the turn; they read a cut sentence. What could break: a wrapping fix that changes the bar's height per beat makes the canvas jump on every step.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the beat sentence is never cut
Before: clip declared on one chrome text node (lanes.css:816-820); clipped width not measured
After: not measured
Method: simulation - three beats walked against the CSS at 900, 1100 and 1440 px; a probe needs the rendered widths, which needs a browser this round does not drive
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none (Lane C: needs a browser to see)

title: Signal's scan animates background-position over the whole sheet
body:
## Summary
The Signal finish's one-shot scan animates background-position (and opacity) on a pseudo-element the size of the sheet for --al-dur-beat (about 3.4 s), a paint on every frame, where DESIGN.md §7 allows transform, opacity and colour only.

## Description
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/lanes.css @keyframes al-scan animates background-position from 100% to -120% on .al-stage[data-preset="signal"] .al-paper::after (inset 0 over the 1170x578 sheet). background-position is not compositable, so the whole pseudo-element repaints each frame of the scan, under a camera transform. DESIGN.md §7: "Transform, opacity and colour only." Registry technique motion/performance-discipline names the same rule. Fixed looks like: a narrow gradient strip translated with transform inside an overflow-hidden .al-paper, same duration and easing, still parked under reduced motion. A lanes.css test can hold every @keyframes to transform and opacity.

## Flow
- Open /?variant=archify-signal; the scan runs once on mount
- Each frame the browser repaints the 1170x578 ::after because background-position changed
- Fix: translateX a strip (will-change: transform) instead; then a lanes.css keyframes test

## Expected impact
Signal readers on modest GPUs see a smoother first scan; the rule the rest of Atlas keeps holds here too. What could break: the sweep's look (its gradient width and travel) must be matched by eye.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - the scan runs on the compositor, not the painter
Before: 1 of 2 keyframes in lanes.css animates a non-composited property (al-scan: background-position); paint count not measured
After: not measured
Method: simulation - the keyframes read from lanes.css; a probe needs a paint-flashing trace in a browser this round does not drive
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none (Lane C: needs a browser to see the sweep match)

title: The lane grid's arrow-key roving has no test
body:
## Summary
Drawing.tsx's onNodeKey implements the lane grid's own roving rule (next occupied cell by lane and column, ties by authored order) inline in a .tsx callback, so no test reaches it.

## Description
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/Drawing.tsx onNodeKey filters NODES by direction and sorts by col*10+lane distance (or the reverse for vertical moves); the header says the grid is half empty and a dense walk would send the reader into nothing. node --test strips TypeScript and not JSX, so the rule is untestable where it lives. Ties exist today: from contracts (tools, col 2) Up, bridge and hooks both score 11 and the authored order picks bridge. A change to NODES order, a new node or a sort tweak silently changes where the arrows go. Registry technique accessibility/keyboard-navigation-models.

## Flow
- Focus a node and press the arrows; the next node comes from onNodeKey's inline sort
- Extract nextNode(id, key, plan) into poses.ts; onNodeKey calls it and focuses the result
- Test: reachability over the 12 nodes, tie order pinned, no-op only at the grid edge

## Expected impact
Keyboard readers keep a stable roving order as the grid changes. What could break: the extraction touches the live key handler, which no test can drive end to end without a browser.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the roving rule is pinned
Before: 0 tests on the roving rule; walked: 3 moves from contracts, bridge and record behave as the header says
After: N of N reachability and tie cases under a gate, once extracted
Method: simulation - three moves walked by hand; the instrument (the extraction plus test) is M and edits the live key path, so it goes to a worker
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/Drawing.tsx onNodeKey: const candidates = NODES.filter(... Math.sign(dCol) === dx ...).sort((a, b) => key(a) - key(b));
key(n) = dx !== 0 ? |dCol|*10 + |dLane| : |dLane|*10 + |dCol|
instrument: extract onNodeKey's candidate search into a pure nextNode(id, key, plan) in poses.ts, then a test that every node is reachable from every other by arrows and no arrow from an occupied cell lands on nothing when a node exists that way

title: The lane sheet's counted claims are typed as words that no test reads
body:
## Summary
"Nineteen systems, twelve nodes", "Eight of the ten drawn story hops are authored edges; two are asserted by README alone", the same sentence in read_turn's note, and the story bar's "/ 12" are hand-typed; all are true today and none is checked.

## Description
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/Chrome.tsx CARDS (card one title, card three item two), examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/turn.ts note ("Eight of the ten drawn hops are runs of this drawing; two are asserted by README alone") and examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/Chrome.tsx StoryBar ("/ 12") restate counts the code computes: SYSTEMS.length 19, NODES.length 12, story.ts TRAIL_COUNTS {hops 10, authored 8, derived 2}, BEAT_VIEWS.length 12 (probed this round). Chrome.tsx calls card three "the receipt: the counts a reader can check against the drawing in front of them", so a drifted count is a receipt that lies. CARDS lives in a .tsx file node --test cannot import, which is why nothing pins it.

## Flow
- Add a node or reroute a hop so TRAIL_COUNTS changes
- The legend and read_turn's hops object update; the receipt card, read_turn's note and the story bar's denominator do not
- Fix: CARDS into copy.ts, the denominator from BEAT_VIEWS.length, a test over the numerals

## Expected impact
Readers and agents who check the receipt against the drawing. What could break: nothing at runtime; copy only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every counted claim is read from the count
Before: 5 counted claims in copy, 0 pinned (all true today: 19, 12, 8/10/2, 12)
After: 5 of 5 pinned once moved
Method: probe - the five claims read and the counts taken from the modules this round; the move is M across Chrome.tsx and copy.ts and was left for a worker
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/Chrome.tsx: title: "Nineteen systems, twelve nodes"
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/Chrome.tsx: "Eight of the ten drawn story hops are authored edges; two are asserted by README alone."
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/Chrome.tsx: `${String(stop + 1).padStart(2, "0")} / 12`
examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/archify-lanes/turn.ts note: "Eight of the ten drawn hops are runs of this drawing; two are asserted by README alone"
probe: TRAIL_COUNTS {"stops":12,"hops":10,"authored":8,"derived":2,"internal":1}; SYSTEMS 19; NODES 12
instrument: move CARDS from Chrome.tsx into copy.ts and add a presets/lanes test that the numerals in the cards, read_turn's note and the story bar's denominator equal SYSTEMS.length, NODES.length, TRAIL_COUNTS and BEAT_VIEWS.length; seed red by changing one
